descriptions.text: T’Ghee Card. Very Rare. Utility Card. Combo. Consumable. You ever mix two completely incompatible foods together to see how they taste? Sometimes it’s great. Like chicken and waffles! Sometimes it’s... a bad idea. Like tuna and haggis. Temporarily combines two monster cards into a single creature. Summoning length is equal to the shorter of the two summoning phases. Post summoning, both monsters are tagged out for the remainder of combat, even if they still have health. Warning: This is a consumable card. It will be destroyed upon use.

recap.text: With The Experience dead, Donut finds a postcard-sized Combo card in its inventory, but Carl cannot hold it, since only the Squad Leader may. Drawn in a hand with no totem, it vanishes in a puff of smoke when she flicks her paw. Katia's gift of a totem, Jola, leaves her one over, so Donut spends the card fusing Uzi Jesus and Asojano into Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, a sickly, sandalled, level 140 figure leaning on his weapon.

beats.headline: In a mob's inventory
beats.text: The Experience is dead, and Donut finds a card thing in its inventory, though she thought cards only came from flagging monsters. It is the size of a postcard, rigid but papery, the Syndicate's logo moving on its back and a red stylised plus floating in a field of stars on its face. Very rare, utility, consumable: chicken and waffles, or tuna and haggis. It fuses two monster cards into one. Carl wonders how rare these really are and tries to put it in his inventory. Cards may only be held by the Squad Leader.
beats.gist: Donut finds a fusing card in a dead mob's inventory, but only the Squad Leader may hold cards.

beats.headline: Discarded, the first time
beats.text: Five cards in the deck, and the totem is not among the four Donut draws: two Time Extends, the Combo card and Stout. A hand without a totem leaves her vulnerable, so Carl tells her to discard or play at once, and with no snare or mystic cards yet, the Combo goes. She flicks her paw downward and it disappears in a puff of smoke, a ten-second timer counting down in the empty space.
beats.gist: Donut discards the Combo card, which vanishes in smoke with a ten-second timer counting down.

beats.headline: Kept in for realism
beats.text: Building the ready deck for the practice arena, Donut does not want the Combo card in it, since it will not be used in practice. Carl thinks it best to keep it in, to make the practice as realistic as possible. A fight can start without warning, so the ready deck has to hold everything they would really carry.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut build the practice arena's ready deck, and Carl keeps the Combo card in.

beats.headline: Two problem cards, one totem
beats.text: From the practice arena Donut reports that they were pretty mad, and Shi Maria too: she wanted the Glow-Up used on her. Before they went into the club, Katia gave Donut one of her excess totems, a mythic creature from Iceland named Jola, and Donut wants him in the active deck, which puts her one totem over. Rather than drop a card, she has used the consumable Combo card to combine two of the problem cards, spent all the utility buffs on them, and made the change permanent with the consumable Glow-Up.
beats.gist: Donut combines two problem cards to fit Jola, then makes the change permanent.

beats.headline: What the Combo made
beats.text: Church organ music, fat digital cherubs and a herd of digital street dogs herald the card Donut made with the Combo: Uzi Jesus and Asojano in one, the most over-the-top reveal of all their cards. What rises from the smoke is a dirty, sandalled, robed figure, hunched and sickly, a green-tinted nimbus round his head and his weapon used as a walking stick. Level 140, like Uzi Jesus. The card names him Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, created via Combo.
beats.gist: Donut's Combo card reveals Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang, a sickly, sandalled level 140 blend of Uzi Jesus and Asojano.
